findings.evidence: `grep -n '^public section' EpsilonEridani/**/*.lean` matches only this file; all other modules use `@[expose] public section`, so `euclideanSection`'s body `LinearMap.range continuation` (line 170) is not in the exported interface.
findings.fix: Add the four missing characteristic lemmas: `continuation_mem_euclideanSection (x) : continuation x ∈ euclideanSection d`, `ofMinkowski_mem_minkowskiSection (v) : ofMinkowski v ∈ minkowskiSection d`, and the eliminations `mem_euclideanSection_iff_exists : z ∈ euclideanSection d ↔ ∃ x, continuation x = z` / `mem_minkowskiSection_iff_exists` (or `euclideanSection_eq_range`/`minkowskiSection_eq_range`). Mark the two intro lemmas `@[simp]`, and consider `@[simp]` on `mem_minkowskiSection_iff`/`mem_euclideanSection_iff` so membership of a concrete image discharges automatically.
findings.issue: `euclideanSection` (line 169) and `minkowskiSection` (line 121) are `def`s under a bare `public section` (line 59, the only non-`@[expose]` section in the repo), so `LinearMap.range` is invisible downstream, yet no intro/elim lemma is provided. Every in-file proof uses the sealed body: `rintro ⟨v, rfl⟩` (128), `rintro ⟨x, rfl⟩` (177), `obtain ⟨x, rfl⟩` (227), `obtain ⟨x, hx⟩` (241). A consumer has no `continuation x ∈ euclideanSection d`, no `ofMinkowski v ∈ minkowskiSection d`, and no way to extract the preimage from membership.

findings.evidence: Lines 174-184: `mem_euclideanSection_iff` is the only membership characterisation, and specialising it at `ofMinkowski v` requires `ofReal_re`/`ofReal_im` plus `Complex.ext_iff` reasoning that no lemma in the file performs.
findings.fix: Add `@[simp] theorem ofMinkowski_mem_euclideanSection_iff {v : Vector d} : ofMinkowski v ∈ euclideanSection d ↔ v (Sum.inl 0) = 0`, and state the obstruction corollary against it so the hypothesis is readable (a nonzero Minkowski vector with vanishing time component is spacelike, hence never light-like).
findings.issue: `causalCharacter_eq_spaceLike_of_ofMinkowski_mem_euclideanSection` takes `hv : ofMinkowski v ∈ euclideanSection d`, and `ofMinkowski_not_mem_euclideanSection` (251) concludes the negation of the same predicate, but nothing characterises when a *real* Minkowski vector lies on the Euclidean section. `mem_euclideanSection_iff` applied to `ofMinkowski v` gives `(↑(v (Sum.inl 0))).re = 0 ∧ ∀ i, (↑(v (Sum.inr i))).im = 0`, i.e. `v (Sum.inl 0) = 0`, which every user must re-derive.

findings.evidence: `mathlib/Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/BilinearForm/Properties.lean:88` `structure IsSymm (B : BilinForm R M)`, with `IsSymm.isRefl` (:100), `IsSymm.restrict` (:116) and `IsSymm.eq_iff` (`BilinearForm/Orthogonal.lean:84`) gated behind it.
findings.fix: Add `theorem complexMinkowskiProduct_isSymm : (complexMinkowskiProduct (d := d)).IsSymm := ⟨complexMinkowskiProduct_symm⟩` alongside the pointwise form.
findings.issue: `complexMinkowskiProduct` is deliberately packaged as a `LinearMap.BilinForm ℂ` for Mathlib interop, but symmetry is exported only unbundled (`complexMinkowskiProduct_symm`), so none of Mathlib's symmetric-bilinear-form API applies without reproving the predicate.

summary: Bodies are correctly left unexposed and the maps `ofMinkowski`, `continuation`, `complexMinkowskiProduct` each carry their `_apply` characterisation, but the two section submodules ship no introduction/elimination API, so downstream consumers cannot produce or consume the membership hypotheses of the headline theorems without re-deriving the witness construction. Symmetry is also only in unbundled form.
